backup.production_rule: Restock screen server support (approved mockup docs/s120/mockup-restock-defaults.html, D-376). Two closed tables (RLS on, no grant to any API role): restock_remembered_amounts (property_id, item_id, amount 0..99, primary key property_id + item_id) and restock_upkeep_checks (kind dish_soap or dish_sponge, changed, check_key unique); the migration seeds one changed = true row per kind and active property so the count starts at the release. Three SECURITY DEFINER functions with an empty search_path, execute for authenticated and service_role only, each needing auth.uid() and submit_cleaning or report_supply on the property (42501 otherwise): restock_context_v1(uuid) returns ok, stock (active consumables), remembered, upkeep_due (3 reports of a turnover kind (turnover, no type, deep_clean as in s110; fee-only rows with submission_id manual-... excluded) on a Manila date later than the session_date of the latest changed = true row; a No never resets; no changed row means not due) and next_tier (returning, regular, vip or null for the earliest confirmed stay with checkin_date >= Manila today; tier only, never a name, id or date); record_restock_v1(uuid,date,text,text,jsonb,jsonb,jsonb) in one transaction requires a usage_key on every row (else 22023), skips replayed usage_key rows, adds up the rows per item and returns ok false, error short_stock, short [...] and writes nothing when one item is over its shelf (an inactive or non-consumable item counts as 0 on the shelf), else calls record_inventory_usage, validates remembered amounts (whole numbers 0..99, active consumables of the property, else 22023) and upserts them only when this call wrote at least one new usage row (a full replay, or a report with nothing used, leaves remembered amounts as they are) and inserts the upkeep answers with the server's Manila date, not the client's (on conflict do nothing; a check_key reused with another property, kind or changed value returns ok false, error check_key_conflict and writes nothing); a full replay returns ok and changes nothing; restock_remind_admin_v1(uuid,uuid) opens one Follow-ups task per item per Manila day through system_task_open_v1, kind restock_reminder, ref item_id:date, title 'is out' and detail 'None left in inventory.' at 0 left (high priority), 'is running out' and 'Only N left in inventory.' otherwise, no cleaner name, no Telegram. No existing function or column changes; one grant is restated, not changed: system_task_open_v1 is revoked from public, anon and authenticated and granted to service_role only (what its own migration already says, so a null ACL cannot leave it open); the restock functions are SECURITY DEFINER and still call it.
backup.notes: Additive. Does not depend on the usage-learning or guest-count releases and applies in any order with them. Old Staff app builds ignore everything here. A report with nothing used leaves remembered amounts as they are; they change only when a save writes a new usage row. record_inventory_usage v3 (20261007112000) and system_task_open_v1 (20260923020000) are called, not changed. restock_reminder is in no closer or sweep list (s102 and s104 sweeps, s117 closers, system_task_close_missing_v1 per kind), so an admin closes it by hand in Follow-ups. The count uses Manila dates, not timestamps, and a Yes is stored with the server's Manila day, so the report that carries a Yes (saved after the restock call) never counts toward the next three; the one remaining limit (a Restock sent just before Manila midnight with its report sent after it counts that report once) is a shortcut noted in the migration. restock_reminder's task is shared per item per Manila day, so a task opened at 5 left keeps its normal priority if the item reaches 0 the same day. Rollback leaves the system_task_open_v1 grant as it is.

rollback.safe_until: Always, with data loss by design: every remembered restock amount and every upkeep answer is dropped. Usage rows written through record_inventory_usage and Follow-ups tasks of kind restock_reminder stay. The system_task_open_v1 grant (service_role only) is not reverted: it only restates what its own migration set.
